newsitem.title: FRANCE: Provisions drive Cie Bancaire into red.
newsitem.headline: Provisions drive Cie Bancaire into red.

text.p: French bank Cie Bancaire announced on Thursday it plunged to a large loss for 1996, hit by heavy provisions to cover exposure to risky property activities.
The bank reported a loss of 1.23 billion francs compared to a profit of 602 million francs in 1995.

The loss included 2.48 billion francs worth of provisions aimed at taking into account "the impact of its accelerated discontinuation of risk-inducing property activities", the bank said in a statement.

Despite the loss, which was in line with forecasts made by the bank in December, it reported "strong growth" in activity and maintained its net dividend at 10 francs, to be paid from retained earnings.

The provisions included 1.03 billion francs to cover all future losses from discontinued activities, including 230 million francs for Sinvim's property development activities, 700 million francs for UCB's loans to property developers and 100 million francs for UCB Socabail Immobiliare in Italy.

There were also 1.10 billion francs in charges to cover exceptional risks related to property loans to businesses granted by UCB through 1993, years during which volumes were particularly significant, and risk "has proven particularly high", the bank said.
It also took a 350 million franc provision to strengthen UCB's competitiveness.
These provisions, it said, should enable Sinvim as well as UCB and its subsidiaries to return to break-even in 1997.
Partly offsetting this, the sale of a six percent interest in Cetelem generated an exceptional capital gain of 980 million francs.
Total new loans written by companies of the Cie Bancaire group totalled 76.0 billion francs, a 17 percent rise over the 1995 level.

Including Findomestic, in which Cetelem alongside the Cassa di Risparmio di Firenze, an Italian savings bank, is the leading shareholder, total new loans amounted to 82.9 billion francs, up 19 percent over 1995.
In France, new loans grew by 15 percent to 66.3 billion francs "with satisfactory margins", the bank said.

Outside of France, new loans amounted to 9.7 billion francs, a 33 percent increase on a constant structural basis. Including Findomestic, new loans totalled 16.6 billion francs, up 38 percent. All areas of activity contributed to the growth.
As of December 31, 1996, total loans managed by group companies amounted to 218.6 billion francs, up 5.1 percent from the 1995 year-end level.
